name: just-code
description: Simple task + sprint board that runs Claude Code per task, with in-card terminals and local PR review/merge

justCode.claudePath.description: Path to the claude CLI (auto-detected if empty)

justCode.maxParallel.description: Tasks in progress at once. Each holds its slot until it is merged, so 1 (default) runs Run all strictly one at a time, in board order, each task building on the previous one's merged work. More runs several side by side in separate worktrees.

enumDescriptions: Ask before edits and commands (approve on the card)
Auto-approve file edits, ask for commands
Claude decides what is safe (its own classifier); asks only when unsure
Allow everything: NO prompts at all. Use only for work you trust

justCode.plannerModel.description: Model for Plan with Claude (alias like opus, sonnet, haiku, or a full model id). Empty = your Claude default.

justCode.taskModel.description: Model for task runs and conflict resolving. Empty = your Claude default.

justCode.autoReview.description: After a branch task's turn ends, an AI reviewer checks its diff. Issues go back to the task to fix, then it is reviewed again.

justCode.maxReviews.description: Failed reviews before the fix loop stops and waits for you.

justCode.autoMerge.description: Merge into the base branch automatically when the AI review passes (not when it flags the change critical).

justCode.reviewCommands.description: Extra command prefixes the AI reviewer may run (e.g. "make test", "flutter test"). Built in: git read commands, common test/build runners, docker compose exec/run, ./gradlew, adb, npx playwright, curl.

justCode.worktreeCopy.description: Gitignored files copied from the project folder into each task's worktree (never committed, never overwritten), so tests that need them run. A worktree only has committed files.

justCode.freshSessionKB.description: Every task has its own fresh Claude session. Review fixes and the continue-after-limit step keep using it, unless its saved transcript is bigger than this many KB: then a new session starts with a short handoff instead, so long tasks don't drag their history into every round. 0 = always start fresh for those steps; -1 = never.

justCode.allowedTools.description: Rules approved for every task without asking, e.g. "Bash(docker compose:*)", "Bash(npm run:*)", "Bash(cd:*)", "Edit". A compound command like `cd x && docker compose exec …` needs a rule for each part. Narrower and safer than 'Allow everything'.
